articles.title: Governo reduz contenção de despesas no Orçamento para R$ 12,6 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Desse total, R$ 304,3 milhões estão bloqueados e R$ 12,3 bilhões contingenciados. Informações constam no relatório de receitas e despesas do quinto bimestre, divulgado nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.summary: Desse total, R$ 304,3 milhões estão bloqueados e R$ 12,3 bilhões contingenciados. Informações constam no relatório de receitas e despesas do quinto bimestre, divulgado nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.body:
A equipe econômica anunciou nesta terça-feira (24) a redução da contenção de gastos do orçamento deste ano, passando de R$ 16,1 bilhões para R$ 12,6 bilhões . Desse total, R$ 304,3 milhões estão bloqueados e R$ 12,3 bilhões contingenciados.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A informação consta no relatório de receitas e despesas do quinto bimestre, divulgado pelos Ministérios da Fazenda e do Planejamento.

Bloqueio e contingenciamento são dois mecanismos previstos no novo marco fiscal para ajustar as contas públicas pelo lado das receitas ou das despesas.

🔎 O governo bloqueia valores do Orçamento quando as despesas aumentam, de forma a manter a meta de gastos do arcabouço fiscal. Já o contingenciamento é feito para cumprir a meta fiscal do governo. O congelamento de recursos do orçamento atinge as chamadas “despesas discricionárias” — ou seja, gastos que não são obrigatórios, como investimentos e salários de servidores.

A redução foi possível porque o governo conseguiu aprovar um projeto de ajuste das contas públicas que permitiu retirar do cálculo para fins de meta fiscal R$ 10,5 bilhões referentes aos subsídios aos combustíveis para atenuar efeitos por causa da guerra no Oriente Médio.

A proposta, aprovada pelo Congresso e sancionada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nesta terça, prevê uma flexibilização das regras fiscais para permitir gastos com subsídios ao diesel, que estão sendo feitos pela guerra no Oriente Médio.

O projeto autoriza o governo a desconsiderar até R$ 10,5 bilhões em despesas extraordinárias para estabilizar os preços do combustível na meta fiscal de 2026. Os recursos estão relacionados à concessão de subvenções econômicas a produtores e importadores de diesel.

A exclusão das despesas da meta fiscal não significa que os gastos deixarão de existir ou de afetar as contas públicas . A medida apenas permite que sejam desconsiderados na avaliação do cumprimento da meta fiscal.

Esplanada dos Ministérios, em Brasília — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Em relação às outras medidas do pacote, o governo explicou que não foram incorporadas no relatório "uma vez que estão sendo objeto de consulta jurídica".

"Portanto, considerando a adoção do limite inferior do intervalo de tolerância da meta de resultado primário para a apuração da necessidade de limitação de empenho e movimentação financeira, conforme previsto no caput do art. 73 da LDO-2026, e o abatimento equivalente ao valor total de R$ 76.984,7 milhões, para fins de verificação do cumprimento da meta, as projeções indicam que há necessidade de limitação de empenho e movimentação financeira no montante de R$ 12.321,8 milhões", explicam as pastas no relatório.

No documento, o governo explicou, ainda, que houve redução de estimativas de despesas primárias obrigatórias , alcançando rubricas como benefícios previdenciários, pessoal e encargos sociais, subsídios e subvenções e Proagro.

O total previsto para essas despesas foi reestimado em R$ 304,3 milhões, o que permitiu o governo desbloquear R$ 2,1 bilhões em comparação ao relatório passado.

➡️Com os ajustes anunciados nesta terça no orçamento, fruto de uma nova projeção para as receitas e despesas para este ano, o governo elevou sua estimativa de déficit nas suas contas de R$ 80,9 bilhões para R$ 89,3 bilhões . Desse montante, pode ficar de fora R$ 76,9 bilhões para fins de apuração de meta fiscal.

➡️Para evitar que a meta de resultado fiscal, de um déficit de até R$ 67,3 bilhões, seja descumprida, foram contingenciados (despesas limitadas) R$ 12,32 bilhões.

➡️Com isso, a equipe econômica passou a estimar um rombo das contas do governo no limite fixado pelo arcabouço fiscal.

Para este ano, a meta é de que as contas do governo tenham um saldo positivo de 0,25% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), cerca de R$ 34,3 bilhões.

De acordo com o arcabouço fiscal, aprovado em 2023, há um intervalo de tolerância de 0,25 ponto percentual em relação à meta central.

Ou seja: a meta será considerada formalmente cumprida se o governo tiver saldo zero, ou se chegar a um superávit de R$ 68,6 bilhões.

articles.title: Al Gore is buying his hometown newspaper
articles.summary: The former vice president, who got his start as an Army journalist and investigative reporter, is set to take over Tennessee’s 113-year-old Carthage Courier.
articles.body:
Al Gore is getting back into the newspaper business after starting his career as an Army journalist.

The former vice president is set to buy the Carthage Courier, his hometown paper in Tennessee, from the family of Hershel and Geraldine Lake, the Courier announced this week. The sale — which is expected to close in the coming weeks — would end the family's 50-year run at the 113-year-old paper.

"When my hometown paper came up for sale, I saw an opportunity to help preserve the Courier as an independent voice for Carthage and Smith County," Gore said in a statement .

The Courier, a weekly newspaper, said it will keep publishing through the transition and retain all of its staff.

Before he ran for Congress in 1976, Gore spent six months as an Army journalist and worked as an investigative reporter for The Tennessean in Nashville. He went on to represent Tennessee in both chambers of Congress, before serving eight years as Bill Clinton's vice president.

Gore won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007 alongside the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and currently resides on his farm in Carthage.

"I look forward to supporting the Carthage Courier team, many of whom have served this community for decades, as they continue to provide vital information and serve this community for generations to come," Gore said.

articles.title: ANÁLISE: investigação de ministros no caso Master vira batata quente | G1
articles.standfirst: Fachin, Polícia Federal e Procuradoria-Geral da República têm adotado movimentos de avanço e recuo, evitando deixar suas digitais em um eventual pedido de investigação.
articles.summary: Por razões distintas, Fachin, PF e PGR evitam assumir a responsabilidade pela formalização de um eventual pedido de investigação de ministros do Supremo.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Ninguém quer segurar a batata quente em que se transformou a possibilidade de investigação de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) no caso envolvendo Daniel Vorcaro.

Se no relatório relativo ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes não há menção ao contrato da mulher dele com Vorcaro, há dúvidas também se, no caso do ministro Dias Toffoli , haverá menção ao Tayayá, resort comprado por uma empresa ligada à teia de negócios de Vorcaro.

Para além das questões pessoais, de quem é amigo de quem, de que ministro é amigo de qual ministro, de quem é mais próximo da Polícia Federal ou da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), ninguém quer ser o responsável pela formalização de um pedido de investigação ou de informações que levem a um pedido de investigação de ministros do Supremo.

Nem Fachin, nem a polícia, nem a PGR. Por razões diferentes, mas não querem.

Se olharmos o primeiro ofício do presidente do Supremo, Edson Fachin , de 2 de outubro, pedindo à Polícia Federal informações sobre os ministros, é um ofício que não chega ao ponto. Fica ali, dizendo, mas não dizendo.

Depois, o ministro afirma que teria orientado a Polícia Federal a incluir as informações relevantes do ponto de vista criminal.

A própria polícia, num primeiro momento, falou em menções e fatos relevantes do ponto de vista criminal. Depois, disse que eram apenas menções a ministros.

Fica todo mundo indo para a frente, recuando, sem querer deixar muita digital.

E agora a bola está com a Procuradoria-Geral da República, que, até aqui, também não atuou no caso de maneira incisiva.

A grande questão é o que a PGR vai fazer com esses relatórios, diante, por exemplo, da falta de informações relevantes no material relativo a Alexandre de Moraes.

Casos que envolvem ministros do Supremo precisam seguir regras da Constituição e do regimento interno da Corte — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

articles.title: Governo Lula tem ao menos oito projetos econômicos para aprovar no Congresso até o fim de 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Congresso tem menos de um mês de trabalhos até o recesso de fim de ano; entre os projetos está Orçamento de 2027 e PEC relacionada a reforma tributária
articles.summary: Congresso tem menos de um mês de trabalhos até o recesso de fim de ano; entre os projetos está Orçamento de 2027 e PEC relacionada a reforma tributária
articles.body:
O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) corre contra o tempo para aprovar uma série de medidas econômicas até o recesso parlamentar, que começa em 23 de dezembro. Em menos de um mês, governistas tentam acelerar a análise de ao menos oito projetos.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Depois da vitória de Lula com a aprovação do ajuste fiscal de R$ 56 bilhões em uma semana , a equipe econômica já estuda enviar ao Congresso uma Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) com mais medidas de ajuste econômico, como mostrou o blog da Ana Flor.

No meio tempo, governistas se voltam para projetos estruturantes e que têm um prazo para entrarem em vigor. São eles:

PEC do IPI (Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados);

Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias (LDO) de 2027;

Definição da alíquota do CBS (imposto sobre consumo da reforma tributária);

Entre os projetos que a aprovação nas próximas semanas são as mais importantes estão textos que precisam estar em vigor no início de 2027 para garantir o bom funcionamento da economia brasileira. Entre eles, as duas medidas que irão determinar o Orçamento de 2027.

A LDO deve ser discutida nos próximos dias. Deputados e senadores precisam aprovar o texto que determina regras para os gastos do governo federal, incluindo metas e prioridades de investimentos para só depois discutir a LOA.

Essa última definirá os investimentos federais, por exemplo, nas áreas de saúde e educação, além de definir quanto será gasto com emendas parlamentares.

Com as eleições, essas discussões foram adiadas. Agora, depois da aprovação do ajuste fiscal, deputados e senadores devem avançar para aprovar as duas leis do Orçamento de 2027 até o recesso em dezembro.

Palácio do Congresso Nacional, em Brasília — Foto: Leonardo Sá/Agência Senado

Em 2027, o novo sistema de impostos do Brasil começa a entrar em vigor. Antes disso, o governo precisa que os parlamentares aprovem a PEC do Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI).

A proposta foi enviada porque a Medida Provisória que estabelece a alíquota do Imposto Seletivo em 2027, também conhecido como "imposto do pecado", leva 90 dias para entrar em vigor.

Até isso acontecer, o IPI deve continuar a ser cobrado de produtos como cigarros e bebidas alcoólicas - e essa cobrança é o que define a proposta do governo.

🔎 Criado pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo, o imposto do pecado começará a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente, como bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros.

A MP do Imposto Seletivo , que também precisa ser votada, prevê a manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano, período de transição. Posteriormente, a partir de 2028, a ideia é que a taxação aumente.

Até 31 de maio de 2027, o governo deve encaminhar ao Congresso um projeto de lei com a definição das alíquotas para serem aplicadas a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2028.

Da mesma forma, há pressa para que o Senado defina a alíquota da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), um dos três tributos criados pela reforma tributária. A alíquota precisa ser definida ainda em dezembro , já que começará a ser cobrada em 2027.

Outra prioridade para o governo Lula é a MP das bets. A medida proíbe a exploração de apostas de quota fixa no Brasil . A proibição já está em vigor no país, mas para continuar após março de 2027, o texto precisa ser aprovado pelo Congresso Nacional.

Para uma medida provisória ser aprovada, é necessário que o texto seja votado antes em uma comissão mista de deputados e senadores. Só depois as votações são feitas nos plenários da Câmara e do Senado.

No entanto, até o momento, a comissão mista não foi nem formada . Líderes do governo já admitem que a análise desta medida de Lula fique somente para 2027.

Já a MP do Desenrola 3.0, que também perde a validade em março, já tem sua comissão mista. No entanto, continua sem previsão de votação.

A nova rodada do Desenrola, programa de renegociação de dívidas de pessoas físicas, é voltado para dívidas de até R$ 10 mil. O governo estima que as dívidas nessas modalidades somem R$ 300 bilhões e pretende alcançar 50% desse valor, ou R$ 150 bilhões.

Apesar das duas medidas ainda terem um prazo mais longo para serem aprovadas pelo Congresso antes de perderem a validade, o governo quer aprovar as medidas ainda neste ano para aproveitar a formação atual da Câmara e do Senado.

A partir de fevereiro de 2027, o PL terá um número muito maior de deputados e senadores . O prazo, no entanto, é curto.

Presidente Lula durante cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto nesta quinta-feira (19). — Foto: Adriano Machado/Reuters

Outra medida que o governo gostaria de aprovar ainda esse ano para fazer o debate sem tantos integrantes da oposição é a regulamentação das big techs .

O projeto do governo Lula cria um órgão dentro do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) que terá a atribuição de regular mercados digitais.

Inicialmente, o texto seria votado na Câmara na semana passada . No entanto, os partidos não chegaram a um acordo sobre o projeto.

O projeto trata de regras de concorrência para as grandes plataformas e não inclui qualquer tipo de moderação de conteúdo para as chamadas big techs . Mas as bancadas partidárias têm dúvidas sobre qual é o tipo de controle que o Cade terá para as plataformas.

A ideia é que o Cade tenha uma superintendência voltada à garantia da livre concorrência e da defesa do consumidor nas relações com as plataformas.

Uma nova tentativa de votação será feita na próxima semana. Caso o governo consiga, deve tentar aprovar o texto no Senado logo em seguida, nos últimos dias de votações no Congresso em 2026.

articles.title: Mullin celebrates Kilmar Ábrego García's self-deportation to Spain: 'We are delighted'
articles.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García voluntarily left the United States for Spain on Tuesday to avoid forced deportation, according to DHS, capping a months-long legal battle with ICE.
articles.body: Kilmar Ábrego García, the illegal immigrant from El Salvador who became a rallying point for critics of President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement policies, voluntarily left the United States on Tuesday to avoid deportation, Fox News has learned. Ábrego García departed for Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday, according to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who celebrated the departure. "We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported from the United States to Spain," Mullin said in a statement Tuesday night. "We promised the American people that this human trafficker, wife beater, gang member, and child predator would not remain in our country. Now, this El Salvadoran man cannot terrorize innocent Americans." He ultimately plans to make his way to Mexico, The New York Times reported, citing his attorneys. TRUMP’S SPECIAL STRATEGY TO DEPORT ILLEGALS GIVES HIM ANOTHER TOOL FOR ENFORCEMENT His departure caps a months-long legal battle that began when he was initially deported to his home country and detained there. A federal judge in Maryland ordered Ábrego García to leave the U.S. by Tuesday, according to two sources familiar with the matter. That order remains under seal, and the exact terms of his release were not immediately clear. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) emphasized that Ábrego García did not receive any financial incentives through the Trump administration's voluntary self-deportation program, which offers migrants travel assistance and financial support to leave the country. "To be clear: Kilmar Abrego Garcia departed the United States pursuant to a removal order. He paid for his own flight and received no incentives,"DHS posted on X. "He will NEVER be allowed back inside the United States." DHS also rejected descriptions of Ábrego García as a Maryland resident. "Kilmar Abrego Garcia is not and will never be a Maryland Man—he is a criminal illegal alien from El Salvador and was a public safety threat to American citizens. He is not coming back, despite the efforts of sanctuary politicians who spent massive amounts of time and money defending this low-life," the department said. The move comes after sustained efforts by the Trump administration to remove Ábrego García, who entered the U.S. illegally more than a decade ago. At one point during the legal proceedings, federal authorities sought to deport him to several African nations. Ábrego García had been living in Maryland with his wife and children when immigration authorities detained him in March 2025. He was subsequently deported to El Salvador in error and held in the Central American nation's maximum-security CECOT prison despite a standing court order barring his removal there due to the risk of gang persecution. Democrats rallied around him despite his suspected ties to the MS-13 gang. "A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego García to rot in a Salvadoran gulag. Today, Kilmar is traveling to a country of his choice, a free man — unharmed and with dignity," said Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who visited Ábrego García while detained in El Salvador. "While the Trump Administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to countries known for human rights abuses, the Administration was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will and the due process rights guaranteed to him and to all in our nation. I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution." MIKE DAVIS: KILMAR ABREGO GARCIA, THE DEMOCRATS' PATRON SAINT OF HUMAN TRAFFICK Federal officials eventually returned him to the U.S. to face human smuggling charges from a 2022 traffic stop in Tennessee. He pleaded not guilty to the charges, which a judge later dismissed. Throughout the legal fight, the administration maintained that Ábrego García was a gang member and pointed to a 2021 protective order his wife had filed against him over domestic violence allegations. articles.title: ICE nabs illegal immigrant days after he claims $1 million Massachusetts State Lottery prize
articles.summary: ICE sources say Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales, an El Salvador man with a 2014 deportation order, ran from officers in East Boston before his arrest.
articles.body: A man who smiled for a Massachusetts State Lottery photo with a $1 million check was arrested by federal immigration officers days later after a brief foot chase in East Boston. Three ICE sources told Fox News that Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales, an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, ran when officers moved in to arrest him early Tuesday but was quickly caught. Multiple officers’ body cameras captured the encounter, the sources said. ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF RAPE, MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES AFTER RELEASE FROM MARYLAND JAIL Velasquez-Morales had been wanted by ICE under a final deportation order issued in April 2014, the sources said. He crossed the U.S. border illegally near Roma, Texas, in 2013, according to the sources. MASSACHUSETTS SUES TRUMP ADMIN TO STOP ICE'S COURTHOUSE ARRESTS: 'UNNECESSARY FEAR' The Massachusetts State Lottery awarded Velasquez-Morales the $1 million prize Nov. 18, and posted a photo on Facebook three days later showing him holding the oversized check. The lottery said he bought The Lottery's winning "$2,000,000 50X Cashword" $10 scratch ticket at a market in East Boston, the same neighborhood where ICE arrested him. The Massachusetts State Lottery says anyone 18 or older can buy a ticket from a licensed retailer. The governor appoints two members of the five-member commission that oversees the lottery. articles.title: Trump's rescue of Nvidia's Huang brings political risks
articles.summary: The US president's intercession to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang has inextricably linked their fates.
articles.body:
After the AI chipmaker Nvidia announced it was bringing back embattled former head Jensen Huang and the company's stock shot up like a bullet, President Donald Trump took a very public victory lap.

"I made the deal," he said during a lengthy phone interview with cable business news channel CNBC.

Trump followed that with an AI-generated image posted to his social media platform that riffed on the famous photograph taken moments after the 2024 attempt on his life in Pennsylvania. But instead of Trump in the image, Huang was the one surrounded by Secret Service guards. It depicted him in front of an Nvidia banner - with a raised fist clenching a red bra.

The post was classic Trump – potentially offensive, yet still a bit opaque.

Was Trump suggesting Huang survived a scandal – one that includes allegations of recklessly jeopardising US national security by consorting with a suspected Chinese spy – the way he had survived an assassin's bullet?

Was the bra a celebration Huang's reported extramarital affairs? By replacing the US flag with an Nvidia standard, was he claiming that America and one of its largest, most powerful companies are one and the same?

At the very least, the image underscores how inextricably linked Huang and Trump now are, with the fate of the former hinging on the successes and failures of the latter.

And with that comes significant risks for the American president and for Republicans, including Vice-President JD Vance, who played a key part in his efforts to rescue Huang.

While Trump has said that a "very thorough investigation" by federal officials "exonerated" Huang and his reinstatement poses no national security threat, that is far from the final word on the matter.

"Every time you have a Chinese woman that's good looking or beautiful, they say she's a spy," Trump told CNBC, adding that "with Jensen, I don't believe that's true".

Democrats and some concerned Republicans in Congress have a different view.

They are promising to launch their own oversight of Huang and Nvidia, with subpoenas and compelled witness testimony, in order to assess whether they violated laws by allowing China to access sophisticated microchip technology.

State governments could also launch their own investigations.

Any new revelations could further damage the company's standing – and, by association, Trump himself.

"I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access," Republican Senator Tom Cotton posted on X.

"Congress has much to investigate," he said.

Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away

What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump

US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation

While Huang has a long record of success at Nvidia, there is no guarantee that he can recapture past glory now that his star his dimmed.

Even if he is free from any criminal liability, the tech mogul is about to be in a much harsher spotlight than he has ever experienced.

Trump also appears to be on the wrong side of public opinion when it comes to AI writ large.

In the recent US midterm elections, candidates on both the left and right campaigned on imposing new restrictions on data centre construction, with many calling for new legal guardrails to prevent AI-fuelled economic and social disruption.

"Rather than addressing the American people's growing concerns about AI, this administration remains asleep at the wheel or willfully ignorant as our most advanced technologies fall into the hands of our greatest competitors," congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a California Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told the BBC.

The president's own political base is also suspicious of the new technology, with rural conservatives often rebelling at the demands that big tech companies have placed on their local resources and civic infrastructure.

The Nvidia story has also exposed rifts in Trump's own administration, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, a China hawk, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, a vocal proponent of AI, publicly feuding over whether to impose new restrictions on AI chip exports.

Both Bessent and Lutnick travelled with Trump on his recent trip to China, although it was the commerce secretary who hitched a ride back to the White House on the Marine One helicopter when Trump returned to Washington last Thursday.

Polling also indicated that political corruption was a top issue for voters this year.

The president's willingness to intervene in the deliberations of a major private company in which he owns millions of dollars of stock could further fuel those concerns.

Trump's decision to help save Huang – noting on Monday that "we have to protect our geniuses, and he certainly is a genius" – could further inflame the public's sense that the rich and powerful, genius or not, play by a different set of rules.

"It almost feels like they've bent the rule, the regulation, to allow this to happen because it's such an important part of our economy right now," Steve Bannon, a former top Trump adviser, said on his podcast on Monday.

"Even in the crash of 2008... I never saw the government step in and take over a board of directors."

For this American president, however, these risks appear to be worth taking because of the stakes involved.

Trump has long viewed the success of the US economy as a key part of his political legacy.

He boasted of the historic growth and low unemployment during his first presidential term (while glossing over the disruptions caused by the Covid pandemic).

And since returning to office, he has celebrated as major US stock indices posted new record highs.

Recent US economic expansion has been fuelled largely by investment in AI technology, and Trump has become one of the industry's biggest boosters.

He scolded states and local governments for blocking data centre construction and predicted that the nation that wins the race for supremacy in AI – which he has tried to rebrand as "super intelligence" – will control the fate of the world.

If Trump views the economy as the key to his political success and AI as instrumental to the health of the US economy, then his dramatic, precedent-shattering actions to try to rescue Nvidia, the company at the centre of America's AI industry, make more sense.

In the weeks since concerns over Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy first surfaced, Nvidia's stock price tumbled more than 32%.

US stock indices tumbled as well, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 10% last week and the larger S&P 500 dropping 8.6%.

The recent financial turmoil may have given Trump a glimpse into a future where AI growth is just the latest financial bubble – like the housing market in 2008 and internet companies in 2001 – that is due for a resounding pop, with similarly dire economic consequences to follow.

Trump's intervention on behalf of Huang arrested that drop, at least for a day.

On Tuesday, Nvidia's stock price gave back much of the bounce it had enjoyed, and larger stock indices were mixed. The fate of the America economy and the AI juggernaut that has powered it is still undetermined.

Trump's intervention may not be a crisis fully averted, but only a crisis delayed.

And if an AI reckoning does come, the US president will be hard-pressed to avoid being caught in the maelstrom.

articles.title: Poll finds US voters want government to end Iran war regardless of terms
articles.summary: New survey finds that 55 percent of voters, including 80 percent of Democrats, want war brought to an end immediately.
articles.body:
A new poll has found that a majority of voters in the United States want an end to the US-Israel war on Iran immediately, even if it means accepting less favourable conditions.

Overall, 55 percent of those surveyed agreed with an “end to the war now, regardless of the terms”.

That number was even higher among Democrats and independents, who agreed with the statement at a rate of 80 percent and 59 percent, respectively. About 25 percent of Republicans said the same.

A majority of Democratic voters also supported steps to pressure the administration of President Donald Trump to stop the conflict.

Fifty-three percent of party members said they would favour Congress withholding funding for military operations, and 51 percent would back an “an Iran war-funding cutoff” in upcoming budget negotiations, even if the manoeuvre risked a government shutdown.

The numbers were published on Tuesday as part of the latest Critical Issues Poll, released by the University of Maryland and the research firm Ipsos.

Shibley Telhami, the poll’s principal investigator, said he was surprised by the level of support for ending the war, regardless of the terms.

“We knew that people were strongly opposed to this war and wanted it to end,” he told Al Jazeera in a phone call. “What we were less sure of is what they would be willing to accept to achieve this.”

The survey asked 1,022 US adults about their perspectives on the war.

In one question, they were tasked with assessing with three options: whether to end the conflict immediately, escalate militarily, or continue on the current path in order to extract concessions from Iran.

Just 21 percent of all respondents favoured the current path, and 18 percent supported escalation.

“Clearly, the public mood is to end it now, whatever it takes,” said Telhami.

Voters also appear sceptical about the US government’s arguments in favour of the war, which include dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme.

The Critical Issues Poll found that only 28 percent of those surveyed believed that the war had left Iran in “worse position” to develop nuclear weapons.

While the US has long voiced concerned that Iran could pursue nuclear arms, intelligence assessments have not found evidence that Tehran has authorised such a step since abandoning its nuclear weapons programme in 2003.

The Strait of Hormuz has also emerged as a key issue, with Iran closing the waterway to commercial traffic early in the war. The Trump administration has responded with a naval blockade in the strait.

Some 20 percent of the world’s oil supply passes through the maritime artery, and fuel prices have spiked as a result of the war.

About 35 percent of respondents in Tuesday’s poll said that they believe Iran is now in control of the strait, while just 12.7 percent said the US is in control.

The poll comes as the Democratic Party is debating how far it should go to end the unpopular war.

In the recent midterm elections , backlash against the war — and as well as related issues like rising fuel prices — contributed to big gains for the Democratic Party.

Trump’s Republican Party, meanwhile, suffered one of its most bruising setbacks in modern US history, losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Members of the Democratic Party’s anti-war left have pointed to the results as proof that voters want an end to the war and an end to US support for Israel.

But that position has brought them into conflict with members of the party’s more hawkish establishment wing.

While leaders such as Representative Hakeem Jeffries and Senator Chuck Schumer have both expressed support for ending the war, they have yet to commit to aggressive strategies to reach that goal.

That includes potentially cutting off funding for military operations against Iran, or using an upcoming funding battle in December to demand that the White House end the war.

“A lot of Democratic figures are dismissing the intensity of public feeling on this issue,” said Telhami. “If they don’t adapt, they will be left behind.”

He added that progressive figures such as Senator Bernie Sanders and Senator Chris Van Hollen have been among those pressing for a more assertive stance.

Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer to lead the Democratic majority in the US Senate, has used the war to portray the party’s moderate leadership as out of step with voters.

The poll found that Democratic voters prefer Van Hollen over Schumer by a ratio of nearly three to one.

articles.title: California prosecutors, victim advocates challenge Newsom's mass death sentence commutation
articles.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom defended commuting 548 death sentences, but victims' advocates and a district attorney call the move morally offensive.
articles.body: California Gov. Gavin Newsom justified his blanket commutation of 548 death sentences to life without parole by arguing that reviewing cases individually would create "two classes of murder victims," a rationale victims' advocates and at least one district attorney called "morally offensive. " Modoc County District Attorney Nina Salarno said Newsom's sweeping action denied the loved ones of murder victims any voice in the clemency process. "I found it really offensive as a victim myself, and [for] my other victims," Salarno told Fox News Digital from Washington, D. C., where she and fellow advocates met with President Donald Trump this week. "There should be individual scrutiny. The individual victims should have a voice. And that's what he has avoided by doing a blanket commutation." CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS SLAM NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW COMMUTATIONS, ACCUSE GOVERNOR OF PUTTING 'POLITICS OVER PEOPLE' "The blanket commutation on a moral level as a victim I find very offensive, but I find the whole thing offensive to our entire rule of law," she added. Topo Padilla, president of Crime Victims United, a nonprofit that advocates for stricter laws against violent offenders, noted that California voters have repeatedly upheld the death penalty at the ballot box, including approving a 2016 measure aimed at speeding up executions. "Here's a guy who throws rocks about kings and protests throughout the streets," Padilla said, referring to Newsom's past criticisms of Trump. "I will promise you, this is a move that is looked at and viewed as a king. He is trampling on the voters." On Monday, Trump vowed to direct the Justice Department to seek the death penalty for child murderers and expedite federal executions as victims’ relatives spoke out at the Justice Department against Newsom's order. SLAIN FIREFIGHTER'S MOTHER PLEADS WITH TRUMP TO INTERVENE AFTER NEWSOM STOPS KILLER'S DEATH SENTENCE "Gavin Newsom and the radical left look at these heinous acts, and their sympathy is not for the children and their parents, but for the monsters who extinguished innocent young lives," Trump said. "He stood with the murderers and child slayers." Justice for crime victims shouldn't be a partisan issue, Padilla said. "Whether you're a Democrat or a Republican, you take politics out of this," he said. "The president of the United States stood up and sounded the alarm. And I hope the country hears it." Newsom's office referred Fox News Digital to news release from Monday featuring victims and survivors who support his decision. GAVIN NEWSOM WIPES OUT CALIFORNIA'S DEATH ROW IN HISTORIC MASS COMMUTATION "As a member of the clergy, I believe that all life is sacred. I also believe in the possibility of redemption. Because of this, I oppose the death penalty," said Rabbi Suzanne Singer, the sister of Michele Reiner and sister-in-law of famed film director Rob Reiner, who were both stabbed to death in December 2025 inside their Los Angeles home. "As a civilized nation, it is barbaric that we still subject people to die at the hands of the state. I am so grateful to Governor Newsom for commuting the death sentences that have been imposed in our state. This is true proof of his moral character." On Nov. 16, a coalition of roughly 30 county district attorneys, law enforcement groups, victims' rights advocates and grieving families filed a petition with the California Supreme Court seeking to halt Newsom's commutations. MICHAEL RUIZ: DA IDENTIFIES 49 LOCAL KILLERS SLATED FOR NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW CLEMENCY — AND THEIR CRIMES Salarno argued that the governor's move disrespects the jurors and judges who endured months-long capital trials. Even though California has not carried out an execution since 2006, Padilla noted that the death sentence itself provides essential legal validation and finality for grieving families, a loss he knows firsthand. "The fact of the matter is the law is the law," Padilla said. "It's like changing the innings in a baseball game, changing from nine to seven retroactively, going back [and] going, 'I know you won that game, but we're going to make it seven innings and now you lost.'" CALIFORNIA DA SAYS GAVIN NEWSOM'S 'CRUEL' DEATH ROW CLEMENCY STABS CRIME VICTIMS 'IN THE HEART' The fight is also deeply personal for Salarno, whose older sister, Catina Rose Salarno, was murdered in 1979 on her first day at the University of the Pacific by her former high school boyfriend, Steven Burns. Following the tragedy, Salarno's mother, Harriet, founded Crime Victims United. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Look, my sister's never coming back, and I understand that," Padilla added. "But I have to accept that she was murdered, like these families have to accept that their loved ones were. And we have to trust the justice system. And now it's been taken away from them. And that's where I think the real issue comes."

articles.title: Trump to Meet With El-Sayed on 'Trumpcare' Pitch
articles.summary: Trump to Meet With El-Sayed on 'Trumpcare' Pitch
articles.body:
President Donald Trump told the New York Post in an Oval Office interview Tuesday that he will meet with Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, a far-left Democrat who wants to put Trump's name on his Medicare for All proposal.

"I know I'll be meeting with him," Trump told the Post, adding, "Maybe there's some place in the middle that we could go."

Trump praised El-Sayed's decision to call the plan "Trumpcare" and gave no date for the meeting.

El-Sayed, who won the endorsement of Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., made Medicare for All a centerpiece of his Senate campaign.

His proposal would create a single government insurance program to cover every American.

El-Sayed pitched the idea directly to Trump on social media this month, posting a mock-up of a gold insurance card bearing the president's name.

Trump shared the image on Truth Social on Saturday without comment, and El-Sayed replied that he was ready to talk, The Washington Post reported.

El-Sayed told NPR earlier this month that he was willing to meet with Trump and cared more about getting the plan passed than what it was called.

With Democrats set to take control of Congress in January, Trump told the New York Post he expects to use his veto power to bring them to the negotiating table and said the two sides could do "great things together," including on healthcare.

Trump also told the Post that "Obamacare hasn't worked" and said he wanted to improve healthcare for Americans.

When he unveiled his healthcare plan in January, Trump argued that the Affordable Care Act sends billions in federal subsidies to insurers while families face rising premiums, according to the White House.

Trump proposed directing federal money into consumers' health savings accounts so they could shop for their own coverage, the White House said.

KFF, a health policy research group, found that premiums for benchmark Obamacare plans rose by an average of 26% for 2026 and are rising another 13% for 2027 before federal tax credits.

KFF also found that the expiration of temporary enhanced tax credits at the end of 2025 drove up what many customers paid for coverage and contributed to a drop in marketplace enrollment from 21.8 million people who paid their premiums in 2025 to 19.2 million in 2026.

articles.body: LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party offered Congress 26 constituencies as seat-sharing negotiations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections stretched to 3.5 hours in New Delhi on Tuesday, with both sides claiming progress but no breakthrough after media reports said Congress tabled a list of 130 of its choice.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav stressed that winnability would guide seat-sharing. That's the biggest responsibility of political parties," he said.SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who headed his party's negotiating team, had made the 26-seat announcement before Tuesday's meeting. These seats include two held by Congress MLAs and four where the party finished second. "There are 20 seats where SP got 70,000 votes while Congress managed 2,000 votes," he said, adding that seat-sharing could not be done at the cost of losing elections.Both parties said they hoped to reach an understanding when negotiations resumed, possibly later this week. articles.title: Judge orders Fulton County to turn over copies of 2020 ballots to Trump-allied election board
articles.summary: The State Election Board, which sets and enforces Georgia’s election rules, is under the control of activists aligned with Trump and his false claims of a stolen election.
articles.body: A state judge on Tuesday ordered Fulton County to turn over unredacted digital copies of 2020 ballots seized by the FBI to the Georgia State Election Board after a two-year fight for the records. The election board, which is controlled by Trump allies, has sought the records over claims by some board members of widespread voter fraud in the 2020 contest won by former President Joe Biden. Fulton County Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe ordered the county to deliver the records to the election board on flash drives by 5 p.m. ET Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving. In her order, she put limits on who can view the records. The State Election Board and Fulton County did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night. The election board, which sets Georgia’s election rules and enforces them in the state, is under the control of Trump-allied election integrity activists. They first subpoenaed the ballots in 2024, months after the board wrapped up an investigation into Fulton County before Trump allies took control of the panel. In December 2025, a state judge said the board could have the records but would need to pay for them. After the FBI seized 600 boxes of 2020 ballots and election records in January, the subpoenas were put on hold until this fall. The county will now be forced to share a digital record the FBI created of those seized documents, and the election board will be required to pay $500 for the request. The amount is considered a small price to pay given the board’s interest in obtaining the records. Georgia was at the heart of President Donald Trump’s 2020 stolen election claims, and Fulton County, which is home to Atlanta and many Democratic voters, was attacked repeatedly by the president. Numerous inquiries and reviews have not found evidence of widespread voter fraud or conspiracy, though some instances of mistakes and errors in election administration have made for frequent targets of criticism from conspiracy theorists. Nationally, the Justice Department has spent much of this year trying to prove Trump’s claims of a stolen election. The DOJ has dedicated significant resources to the effort but has struggled to substantiate the president’s insistence of widespread voter fraud. Instead, it has brought a number of indictments against the small number of people who voted without U.S. citizenship.

articles.title: Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
articles.summary: The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has sparked bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO. “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night. Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.” “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said. A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity. “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. In Congress, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are preparing to grill Huang over their national security concerns. A spokesperson for the Republican-led House Intelligence Committee told NBC News that Huang’s reinstatement “changes nothing” and that there “are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers.” Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter are expected to sit for transcribed interviews next Tuesday and Wednesday before the House Select Committee on China, the House Intelligence Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee. Huang, who has not been charged with a crime, resigned from his post as CEO of the chip giant following reports that he had a relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. In a Nov. 8 memo to Nvidia’s staff, he said, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Trump worked behind the scenes over the weekend to get Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. That move has been met with bipartisan backlash. Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., on Monday raised concerns over Nvidia’s quick reversal to rehire Huang after indicating it wouldn’t. “His own board described his behavior as lacking ‘candor.’ I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement,” Ricketts wrote in a post on X. Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., wrote that with Nvidia’s rehiring of Huang, “the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens.” Cramer and Ricketts are both members of the Senate Banking Committee, where Huang is scheduled to testify in public Dec. 3. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social post that the U.S. government “has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” Similarly, Nvidia’s board said it reached the decision to reinstate Huang after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

articles.title: Florida AG calls for doctor to lose medical license over 149 alleged illegal abortions
articles.summary: Florida's attorney general is pushing to revoke a North Miami Beach doctor's medical license, citing suspected violations of the Heartbeat Protection Act.
articles.body: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is pushing to strip a North Miami Beach doctor of his medical license over at least 149 suspected illegal abortions, a number he says could rise to 180 as the investigation continues. Uthmeier said in a video posted by his office on X that preliminary reports from state health officials indicate Dr. Sylvester Braithwaite allegedly performed the procedures between June 2024 and September 2026. He said some may have been late-term abortions and called on the Florida Board of Medicine to revoke Braithwaite’s license. DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH "A medical license is not a license to break the law," Uthmeier said. Uthmeier cited Florida’s Heartbeat Protection Act and said none of the cases fell under the exceptions he outlined for medical emergencies or victims of rape, incest or human trafficking. He said each alleged violation amounts to a third-degree felony. "My office is investigating this conduct, and we will follow the facts wherever they lead," Uthmeier said. "And we will prosecute doctors who ignore our laws." Noah Brandt, executive vice president of the anti-abortion group Live Action, told Fox News Digital that Braithwaite should lose his medical license for good and face prosecution if investigators confirm the allegations. "If these allegations are true, at least 149 innocent preborn children were killed in direct violation of Florida law, and each of those children deserves justice," Brandt said. "The killing of innocent human beings, including through abortion, should be illegal, and the fundamental human rights of every person, born and preborn, must be protected under the law." ‘YOU’RE FIRED’: NEARLY 40 PRO-LIFE GROUPS URGE TRUMP ADMIN TO CUT OFF PLANNED PARENTHOOD FUNDS Brandt said Braithwaite should be "prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law" if the allegations are proven. He also praised Uthmeier for "his commitment to enforcing Florida’s pro-life laws and setting an example for attorneys general across the country." Florida state Rep. Taylor Yarkosky backed Uthmeier in a reply on X, calling the alleged conduct "the Devil at work" and thanking the attorney general "for upholding the law in Florida, and mostly for protecting the lives of the unborn!" Uthmeier did not say whether any charges had been filed or how far along the pregnancies were in the cases he described as potentially late-term. Braithwaite is a board-certified obstetrician and gynecologist who serves as medical director of Women & Teens Healthcare in North Miami Beach, according to his professional biography. articles.title: These young Republicans have a message for their party: it's time to "grow up"
articles.summary: FORT WORTH, Texas (AP) — Three weeks after midterm elections that devastated the Republican Party, several dozen of its more youthful members gathered at a b...
articles.body:
FORT WORTH, Texas (AP) — Three weeks after midterm elections that devastated the Republican Party, several dozen of its more youthful members gathered at a brewery on Monday night to sort through the pieces.

The meeting was organized by the Tarrant County Young Republicans, a local organization on the frontlines of a national reckoning. Their last leader resigned shortly before the midterms because she couldn't bring herself to vote for some of her party's candidates. Then their county, once a conservative stronghold, flipped blue.

"Everyone has someone to blame, and that finger is never pointed at ourself," said Derrick Wilson, who heads the Texas Young Republican Federation, a coalition that includes the Tarrant County chapter. "So we're going to have to get past that and figure out, what did we do wrong?"

Democrats won the U.S. Senate race and the governor's office in Texas, their first statewide victories in over three decades. There's no consensus about the path forward, but several people at this week's meeting gave similar answers.

Some are bored with "owning the libs" and put off by meme-driven political messaging that they see as flippant in the face of real challenges. Many felt President Donald Trump didn't follow through on his promises. And others gave similar advice to their party leaders: "grow up," "take themselves seriously" and "be humble."

Some Republicans saw no progress on affordability

The event opened with someone introduced by Wilson as a "survivor" of the midterms. State Appeals Court Judge Brian Walker, a Republican who won reelection, gave a withering assessment of how the party had stumbled down the wrong path with Trump-style belligerent politics led by the "loudest" and "craziest" voices.

Robert Coe, a mustachioed 29-year-old in a black cowboy hat, murmured in agreement as Walker spoke.

Coe voted for Trump three times, and now gives the Republican Party an approval of four out of 10 after seeing little progress on affordability.

"Me and millions of other Americans are just tired of that, and we're not seeing any viable solution to it," he said. "It's almost as if the people in power don't even want to try and solve it."

Coe, who still voted for Republicans in the midterms and was the one who wanted party leaders to "grow up," has been put off by "the high school level name-calling, the infighting on an almost childish level." Citing Trump's screeds against talk show hosts, Coe said "there is no decency."

Another attendee who nodded through Walker's remarks was Andrew Gochis, a 29-year-old coach and teacher who has worked in politics. He voted for a mix of candidates rather than just Republicans.

He said Republicans had conflated being respectful and being weak. The party has to "do better," he said, at standing on their principles of deportations or opposition to abortion while also treating people such as immigrants or women who get abortions as "a human being that has value."

"The Republican Party needs to get meaner," said Stephen Nesbitt, a 26-year-old former U.S. Marine. "We need to get stricter, we need to triple down." He listed non-Christians, immigrants and communists as the "enemy."

His view meshes with some who believe the Make America Great Again Movement didn't go far enough, but he was an outlier among those interviewed at Monday's meeting.

Wilson, the chair of the state organization, wants the party to "return to its roots" of "fiscal and social conservatism." He and the organization are currently in "listening mode" to be better prepared ahead of 2028, a strategy that he felt was missed before the midterms.

"Young people wanted to buy homes and start families," he said, "then they look on the news and they see Trump say, 'I don't want housing prices to go down, I want them to go up.'"

Trevor Carr, 25, attended the meeting for the first time because he saw the midterm elections as a repudiation of the party's old guard and he wanted to have a role in its future.

Carr didn't vote in the midterms because he doubted Trump was going to fulfill his promises, and he wants to see a party less focused on loyalty to one man and one that clings more closely to an ideologically sound platform.

While Carr said Trump's approach was once helpful for shaking up the system ten years ago, "it's served its purpose, and it's time to move on to be a serious political movement."

articles.summary: Colau responde a Albiol contraponiendo la gestión de vivienda pública en Alicante, Madrid y Badalona con la suya en Barcelona
articles.body: La réplica de Ada Colau a Xavier García Albiol desplazó el debate entre ambos en 'La Sexta' sobre la "inseguridad jurídica" hacia las políticas de vivienda pública, poniendo bajo escrutinio gestiones vinculadas al Partido Popular y contraponiendo los datos de Barcelona frente a Badalona. Al tomar la palabra tras la intervención de su interlocutor, Colau recogió el argumento y lo trasladó a ejemplos concretos de acceso y gestión residencial. En su intervención, Colau señaló de entrada: "Yo le he escuchado. Me habla de la inseguridad jurídica y también quería hablar yo de la inseguridad jurídica, por ejemplo, la que sufren los vecinos y vecinas de Alicante, gobernado por el Partido Popular, donde la primera promoción pública de VPO que se ha hecho en veinte años, que no se hacía vivienda pública, ha sido adjudicada a cargos políticos y a familiares del Partido Popular. Eso genera inseguridad jurídica". A continuación, amplió el foco crítico hacia la Comunidad de Madrid y la gestión de su presidenta al afirmar: "Otra gran inseguridad jurídica, que la señora Ayuso, gran representante de su partido, que entiendo que para usted es un referente también en materia de vivienda, pues hace muy poca vivienda pública, luego se la regala a los fondos buitres y encima se compra un ático de más de seis millones de euros con dinero público. A mí eso me genera muchísima inseguridad jurídica". Pasando al balance de su etapa al frente del consistorio barcelonés, Colau defendió el crecimiento del parque público y detalló los mecanismos empleados: "Y usted mencionaba Barcelona. Déjeme que le explique que en Barcelona, en solo ocho años, duplicamos el parque de vivienda público por diferentes vías. Y entonces le decía, eso que le estaba explicando yo antes, efectivamente, yo en Barcelona lo he hecho: a través del tanteo y retracto, 1600 viviendas que eran de grandes propietarios pasaron al parque público en régimen de alquiler social; hicimos mil viviendas en régimen cooperativo, viviendas de construcción pública, y con todo eso 7500 viviendas en ocho años". Finalmente, Colau cerró su réplica estableciendo una comparación directa con la gestión municipal de Albiol en Badalona: "Usted en ocho años en Badalona, cero viviendas públicas. Entonces, si vamos a contrastar modelos, pongamos también estas cifras sobre la mesa".

articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, y su pronóstico electoral: "La remontada del PSOE no la veo por ningún lado; es irreconocible"
articles.standfirst: El analista afirma que el discurso socialista moviliza a los votantes de derecha
articles.summary: El analista
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos ha analizado algunos pronósticos electorales que vaticinan un acelerón del PSOE durante los últimos días antes del 29 de noviembre. "La remontada del PSOE no la veo por ningún lado. Observo que muchas personas, entre ellas bastantes socialdemócratas, quieren pasar página y están a favor de un cambio de gobierno. El actual PSOE es irreconocible para los que ya tenemos unos años", ha afirmado en sus redes sociales. El profesor universitario, de hecho, ha asegurado que la insistencia de algunos dirigentes socialistas en el posible acelerón del partido en los comicios generales pueden generar un efecto rebote. "Dicen una y otra vez que van a remontar. Al hacerlo, están haciendo una gran propaganda al PP", ha señalado. Gonzalo Bernardos ha explicado que esta actitud puede movilizar más a la derecha: "Muy pocos se abstendrán". Además, el analista catalán ha augurado que esto provocará que determinados electores apuesten por el Partido Popular como el "voto útil" este 29N. "Los antiguos votantes del PSOE, que quieren cambio de Gobierno, harán que opten en mayor medida por el PP que por la abstención o el voto en blanco", ha añadido en su publicación en X, antes Twitter. Por otra parte, Gonzalo Bernardos ha criticado la evolución del PSOE. "En esta red, algunos tuiteros mi criticaron porque dije que el PSOE se había convertido en un partido populista de extrema izquierda. En la campaña electoral, las múltiples medidas copiadas al Frente Amplio así lo confirman", ha planteado, citando un artículo de opinión del ABC en el que se critican algunas medidas del PSOE para "comprar votos" en el último tramo de la campaña. El economista también ha lanzado un dardo a la candidata de Frente Amplio, Ada Colau: "!Qué gran error cometió el Frente Amplio cuando eligió a Ada Colau como cabecera de cártel! No tiene ninguna credibilidad, no inspira confianza y ni tan solo es ocurrente como lo es Gabriel Rufián. No sé qué hace encabezando una candidatura estatal una independentista catalana.

articles.title: Oskar Matute da con la pregunta incómoda para PNV tras admitir que no pactan con Vox: "El PP de Ayuso y Tellado, ¿ese sí?"
articles.standfirst: El debate enfrenta al dirigente de EH Bildu y a Maribel Vaquero sobre pactos y derechos
articles.summary: El debate enfrenta al dirigente de EH Bildu y a Maribel Vaquero sobre pactos y derechos
articles.body: El intercambio entre Oskar Matute y Maribel Vaquero en el debate vasco para el 29N ha puesto el foco en el alcance de los pactos políticos y en el papel del Partido Popular respecto a Euskadi. En medio del debate, el dirigente de EH Bildu ha planteado sus dudas sobre los límites de los acuerdos y ha interpelado directamente a la representante del PNV. Matute ha comenzado su intervención marcando una posición compartida sobre la extrema derecha y el equilibrio de apoyos parlamentarios, pero evitando importar tensiones externas al debate vasco. "Yo casi me surge un interrogante. Bien, con Vox nada y eso lo compartimos todos. Creo que los votos del PNV eran tan necesarios como los de cualquiera para sumar más de 175, no hay valor. Nosotros hablamos con todo el mundo, pero yo quiero no discurramos, no hagamos, no entreguemos el clima de Madrid aquí, que ayer yo creo que dimos una lección portándonos de manera correcta", se refería al debate a ocho de RTVE. A continuación, ha trasladado su duda hacia la posibilidad de entenderse con un Partido Popular marcado por figuras como Isabel Díaz Ayuso, Miguel Tellado y Alberto Núñez Feijóo. "No, pero a mí me surge ahí una pregunta. Es decir, ¿pero con el PP en solitario sí? Es decir, el PP de Ayuso y de Tellado, ¿ese sí supone una puerta de avance para la sociedad vasca, para todo eso que hemos dicho y que yo creo que hemos compartido en buena medida, mucha, la mayoría de los que estamos aquí, de lo que sería bueno para Euskadi y lo que no sería bueno para la sociedad de Euskal Herria? Es decir, yo creo que ahí hemos sido bastante claros. Y, sin embargo, esa duda hay de con Tellado y con Ayuso, es decir, con ese Feijóo que vive atemorizado por la presión que le metan estas dos célebres personas de la democracia liberal, ¿qué dirán ellos? ¿Sí? Yo creo que no, sinceramente, pero es un interrogante que me ha surgido." Tras las réplicas de Vaquero sobre el veto a Vox y la defensa del autogobierno, Matute ha replicado señalando lo que, a su juicio, se desprendía de las palabras de su interlocutora y precisando el sentido de su interés en el debate. "Tampoco sé si a los demás le dijimos que sí, porque eso es lo que has dejado entrever. Y me parece, ¿eh?" Además, ha añadido: "No, pero vamos, que por aclarar, o sea, no es una cuestión que a mí me interesa especialmente, yo creo que me interesa como vasco." Finalmente, ante la invitación de Vaquero a trasladar la discusión a otro momento, Matute ha cerrado su intervención rebajando el tono de confrontación directa pero insistiendo en la responsabilidad política de los dirigentes del PP. "Simplemente quiero decir a la gente que no voy a discutir contigo, de verdad. Simplemente quiero aclararle a la gente que Miguel Tellado es del Partido Popular, que la señora Ayuso es representante del Partido Popular y que Feijóo, lo que dice, también es del Partido Popular, y que no parece que sea fácil garantizar derechos con la agenda que traen, sin más. La gente sabe."

articles.title: Tuberville suggests Texans 'flee the woke-show' for Alabama after blue wave midterm elections
articles.summary: Alabama Gov.-elect Tommy Tuberville is inviting Texas residents and businesses to "flee the woke-show" for his state after Democrats swept every statewide race in Texas.
articles.body: Alabama Sen. Tommy Tuberville, who is set to become the state's next governor in January, invited Texas residents and businesses to "flee the woke-show" and move to Alabama after historic Democratic gains in the Lone Star State during the midterm elections earlier this month. "To any red-blooded patriot or business wanting to flee the woke-show that is coming to Texas… Alabama is open for business," Tuberville, a Republican, wrote Monday on X. Tuberville was responding to a video shared by Libs of TikTok, an account run by a conservative influencer, that appears to show an event hosted by Equality Texas, a pro-LGBTQ+ advocacy group. DAN PATRICK CONCEDES TEXAS 'TURNED PURPLE' AFTER DEMOCRATS' HISTORIC BLUE WAVE "Texas is Black. Texas is gay. Texas is trans. Texas is indigenous. Texas is lesbian. Texas is all of us," the speaker is heard saying in the clip. "Never, never forget that the 'T' in Texas stands for trans," the speaker continued. This comes after Democrats swept statewide races in Texas and flipped the governor’s office, a U.S. Senate seat and the Texas House, while Republicans managed to maintain control of the Texas Senate. TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES Gov. Greg Abbott, who was vying for a fourth term, lost in his re-election bid to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick lost his re-election to Democrat Vikki Goodwin and Texas Attorney General and U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton was defeated by Democrat James Talarico, contributing to huge Democratic gains in the state and across the country. Democrats won every statewide race in Texas, bringing an end to decades of Republican control in contests that had once been considered sure bets for the GOP and leaving U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz as the only Republican holding statewide elected office. With those key victories, Texas will be under Democratic control for the first time in more than three decades.
