Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) to become the next Senate majority leader. “I’ve talked with Mainers about what they need from the Senate, and I believe it’s time for a change in leadership. I’ll be voting…
articles.body:
Troy Jackson, the progressive senator-elect from Maine who defeated Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), announced Wednesday that he will support Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) to become the next Senate majority leader.

“I’ve talked with Mainers about what they need from the Senate, and I believe it’s time for a change in leadership. I’ll be voting for Sen. Van Hollen,” Jackson announced in a statement shared online.

He cited Van Hollen’s support for ending the Senate filibuster, passing “Medicare for All” and raising the federal minimum wage as factors behind his decision.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

“When we spoke, I told him Maine needs a seat at the table when the caucus decides what gets funded and what we’re going to fight for,” Jackson continued. “I came away confident he’ll take Maine’s priorities seriously.”

His support gives Van Hollen at least seven votes in the contest to become Senate majority leader. The Maryland Democrat needs at least 29 votes to beat Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.).

Schumer has claimed for weeks that he’s already locked down the votes to be elected as majority leader next Congress, but Van Hollen insists it’s still a “wide-open race.”

The incumbent leader recruited Maine Gov. Janet Mills (D) to run against Collins in the Maine Senate race, but she lost the Democratic primary to progressive populist Graham Platner, an ally of Jackson’s.

Jackson stepped in as the Democratic Senate nominee after Platner dropped out of the race amid allegations of sexual assault by a woman he formerly dated.

The senator-elect and Platner shared many of the same policy goals and both ran on shaking up the party establishment in Washington.

Jackson said he and Van Hollen both support bringing bold change to the Senate.

“Sen. Van Hollen and I agree that it’s time to end the filibuster, pass Medicare for All, and give working people a raise by increasing the minimum wage. I want a leader who’ll bring those fights to the floor,” he wrote.

Two other progressive senators-elect, Abdul El-Sayed (Mich.) and Peggy Flanagan (Minn.), have also declared their support for Van Hollen.

articles.title: Forest Service releases 1982 report on ‘Bigfoot’ tracks found in Oregon
articles.summary: The United States Forest Service recently released a report detailing a 1982 investigation into a reported sighting of bigfoot tracks in the Umatilla National Forest.
articles.body:
PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) – The U.S. Forest Service recently released a report detailing a 1982 investigation into a reported sighting of Bigfoot tracks in the Umatilla National Forest.

The report dates back to June 18, 1982, and describes an investigation led by USFS Biologist Rodney Johnson, who conducted an on-site investigation into reported Bigfoot tracks in the Mill Creek Watershed.

According to Johnson, if the tracks were faked, someone went through “a great deal of trouble,” to make the tracks in the forest.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The report investigates tracks at three locations, labeled “Site A,” Site B” and “Site C.”

Two of the “bigfoot” tracks were located near the Low Creek Trail, and another track was found near an unnamed trail at the top of Low Ridge.

The tracks at “Site A” were about 1.5 miles above Mill Creek in the Low Ridge Trail and extended down the trail about 25 feet. In the report, Johnson said plaster casts were made out of two of the tracks along the trail as the other tracks were too faint to copy.

Tracks at “Site B” were found near a bog next to the Low Creek Trail about 2.5 miles above Mill Creek. That site showed about 18 prints over a distance of about 40 feet.

Meanwhile, the team did not visit the third site because of the conclusions made at “Site B,” and because of the time of day they would have reached the site.

“Based on several things, it is my opinion that the tracks observed at Site ‘A’ and Site ‘B’ along Low Creek were made by something other than a 300-pound plus two-footed being,” the Forest Service report says.

In the report, Johnson gave several reasons why he believed the tracks did not belong to the creature.

First, “the stride of the tracks did not change with slope,” the report says, noting the stride of all the tracks was four feet.

“The tracks were on approximately a 2-3 percent grade on Site ‘A’, and approximately 8-25 percent on Site ‘B’. Under this range of slope the stride should have changed somewhat (shorten on uphill grade, lengthen on downhill grade, etc.) This was not the case at both sites,” the report says.

Second, the tracks did not sink to the bottom of the mud. The biologist noted his boots were sinking deeper in mud at the same location as the tracks.

Third, the tracks were “isolated,” or not connected to a trail and had a definite beginning and end. “The numerous bear trails we observed could very easily be followed,” the report stated. “This was not the case with the ‘Bigfoot’ tracks.”

Additionally, at Site B, it appeared that forest litter, such as needles, were brushed aside before the track was made. “It was obvious that the litter had been displaced sideways from the track area in an unnatural manner,” the report says.

Investigators also found that the small toe prints lacked a definite “pad” at the tips, as expected on Bigfoot, and noted there were no signs of heel or toe slippage on steeper areas. Investigators also said it appeared that the prints were made by a foot rocking back and forth on the trail to make the track.

“If the tracks were faked, someone went to a great deal of trouble and detail. The ‘print’ marks on the foot would have to be very hard to duplicate. They appear very natural. I would almost suspect a case made of an actual foot would have had to be used to make the ‘fake’ feet. If this were the case though, the other creases in the foot should have shown,” the report says.

This report was followed by a memo sent to Forest Service District Supervisor Wayne Long, from a U.S. Border Patrol member in Bellingham, Wash.

“My opinion is that the tracks were a very clever attempt to penetrate a hoax, involving your office of agency, in order to lend authenticity or credibility to the general public,” the memo states.

According to the memo, the tracks appeared to have been made by soft plaster or a “rubber-coated foot.”

“Who made the tracks — my opinion, someone with normal access to the area, very knowledgeable and interested in ‘bigfoot’ legends and stories; a person large enough to implant the track device,” the memo said.

The report, and memo were publicly released in October — 44 years after the investigation. Officials explained to KOIN 6 News that the Forest Service releases reports like this to its National Reading Room if requests for the documents are made at least three times.

Officials tell KOIN 6 that the Forest Service “routinely” received reports related to Bigfoot.

In a statement shared with the outlet, a spokesperson for the United States Department of Agriculture — which oversees the Forest Service — said, “Stories of Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and other legendary creatures have long been part of the cultural fabric of the Pacific Northwest and continue to add to the rich tradition of folklore that surrounds our public lands.”

The spokesperson added, “While the Forest Service does not endorse or make any claims regarding the existence of such creatures, we appreciate the public’s enthusiasm for exploring and learning about our public lands.”

articles.title: Vance blames Obama for toxic lead threat in Iowa
articles.summary: Vice President Vance blamed former President Obama for the toxic lead risk in Iowa resulting from the Army’s detonation of a cache of explosives Wednesday. “The can had been kicked down the road. If you go back to 2009 under the Obama administration, we stored this highly unstable stuff with no real plan for how…
articles.body:
Vice President Vance blamed former President Obama for the toxic lead risk in Iowa resulting from the Army’s detonation of a cache of explosives Wednesday.

“The can had been kicked down the road. If you go back to 2009 under the Obama administration, we stored this highly unstable stuff with no real plan for how to move it, with no real plan for how to neutralize it,” Vance told reporters in Ohio, referring to the stockpile of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa.

“We became aware — meaning in the Trump administration — we became aware that there really wasn’t a good option here about six months ago,” he continued. “It was impossible to move it. It was impossible to effectively neutralize it without causing significant danger to the surrounding communities.”

Vance said the administration was left with two options: to conduct a controlled detonation or “to just let it sit there.”

“Every scientist, every expert that we talked to, said that if you let it sit there, there’s a very good chance, whether it’s tomorrow, a week from now, a month from now, but very soon there is a very good chance that with the cold weather this stuff is going to detonate on its own,” he said, adding that an uncontrolled detonation worried the administration.

Critics have raised concerns over how the situation was able to escalate to the point where lead azide-containing weapons were at risk of exploding.

Locals residing close to the detonations and public health experts have raised concerns about the impact lead exposure from the detonation could have on people — especially children — as well as livestock.

Lead exposure in children can result in brain damage, nervous system damage, learning problems, behavioral issues and a lower IQ.

It can also cause seizures, coma and death in rare cases, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

articles.title: Vance says Blanche assured him Huang ‘under no investigation’
articles.summary: Vice President Vance said Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche assured him Jensen Huang was not under investigation as the administration pushed for the ousted Nvidia CEO’s return to the company. “We were told he was under no investigation,” Vance told reporters in Ohio. “Frankly, in our country, we have to remember we don’t try…
articles.body:
Vice President Vance said Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche assured him Jensen Huang was not under investigation as the administration pushed for the ousted Nvidia CEO’s return to the company.

“We were told he was under no investigation,” Vance told reporters in Ohio. “Frankly, in our country, we have to remember we don’t try people in the court of public opinion. We don’t try people based on anonymously sourced stories in The New York Times. We try people based on evidence.”

Huang, who returned to his CEO post on Monday, has admitted to having multiple affairs, including with another Nvidia executive and a woman, Alice Huang, suspected of working with China’s intelligence agency.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Alice Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm suspected of helping funnel Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.

When pressed on who gave him assurances that Jensen Huang was not under investigation, Vance pointed to Blanche and others in the U.S. government.

Blanche did not clearly say whether Jensen Huang had been under investigation when asked by reporters on Tuesday.

“What does that mean? Had Huang been investigated? For what?” Blanche said about the Nvidia CEO. “I don’t understand the question … even the reporting from the various leaks or sources or whatever that was out there didn’t suggest Huang himself was under some sort of investigation. At least not that I saw.”

Blanche previously said the FBI was “looking into” allegations related to Jensen Huang. He said Tuesday that did not necessarily mean a formal investigation had been launched.

The Justice Department and the Commerce Department have confirmed they are investigating Megaspeed, the firm where Alice Huang previously worked.

Vance was a part of President Trump’s push to reinstate Jensen Huang at Nvidia following his decision to step down earlier this month.

Trump said Monday that Blanche had no reason to believe Jensen Huang’s return to the company posed any national security risks to the country.

Still, Republicans and Democrats have signaled they still have concerns about Jensen Huang’s return, the role the administration played in it and whether the billionaire divulged any secrets or was aware of export violations.

Jensen Huang is set to testify before House and Senate committees next week.

articles.title: Second judge invalidates Trump’s new attempt to restrict birthright citizenship
articles.summary: A second federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempts to restrict birthright citizenship. U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper of Washington, D.C. ordered a preliminary injunction in a 67-page memorandum opinion, in which he asserted the Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment “promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United…
articles.body:
A second federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempts to restrict birthright citizenship.

U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper of Washington, D.C. ordered a preliminary injunction in a 67-page memorandum opinion , in which he asserted the Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment “promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States.”

The judge also said the court will prevent federal authorities from enforcing the president’s August executive orders, which sought to limit the scope of birthright citizenship and combat “birth tourism” — which involves traveling to another country for the primary purpose of giving birth on its soil so the child automatically has citizenship.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Cooper added the order also seeks to keep the Trump administration “from taking any other actions to deny or infringe on the citizenship of class members.”

“It goes without saying that the public interest is always served by having federal agencies follow the Constitution and federal law,” Cooper, an Obama appointee, wrote.

The order came after immigrant’s rights advocacy groups , including the American Civil Liberties Union , filed a lawsuit in September challenging the president’s orders.

“The merits in this case are clear-cut,” Cooper’s memo read. “The Supreme Court has twice confirmed that all children born in this country are U.S. citizens, save only for the small handful who are not subject to U.S. law.”

In September, Maryland U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman also blocked the administration’s efforts via preliminary injunction following a challenge two other immigration rights groups.

“This Court must, once again, preliminarily enjoin enforcement of the President’s most recent attempt to strip the right to citizenship from them,” Boardman, a Biden appointee, wrote.

Earlier in June, the Supreme Court in a 6-3 vote struck down Trump’s earlier executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which was among his Day 1 policies after retaking the White House.

articles.title: Miller touts Iowa blast as ‘tremendous display of unity’ under Trump
articles.summary: White House chief of staff Stephen Miller praised the U.S. Army’s lead-based munitions detonation in Iowa on Wednesday as a success by the Trump administration, as early reports suggest the spread of lead pollution is lower than expected. “Every single extraordinary mitigation measure put into place far exceeded expectations, and the technical mastery of the…
articles.body:
White House chief of staff Stephen Miller praised the U.S. Army’s lead-based munitions detonation in Iowa on Wednesday as a success by the Trump administration, as early reports suggest the spread of lead pollution is lower than expected.

“Every single extraordinary mitigation measure put into place far exceeded expectations, and the technical mastery of the army technicians in directing the controlled blast downward into the earth … demonstrates that the U.S. Military’s engineering prowess is truly second to none,” Miller wrote in a lengthy post to the social platform X.

The Army performed a controlled detonation of the decades-old, lead azide-containing munitions over fears that natural factors, like weather, could cause them to explode inadvertently and release lead into the air. Lead is toxic, and there is no safe amount humans can tolerate without adverse effects.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Officials used several mitigation factors, including a “water wall,” to reduce the amount of particulate matter that entered the air. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said in a Wednesday social media post the Environmental Protection Agency’s sensors were not detecting any readings of lead in the air nearly an hour after the blast.

The lead munitions were gathered up and stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in 2009, and in March, they were said to be crystallizing — making them particularly volatile. And as some are now questioning how the Army let the munitions reach this state in the first place, Miller blamed the Obama administration.

The chief of staff praised President Trump, Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds (R) and Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) for how they managed the detonation process.

“President Trump’s leadership team leapt into action and, through intricate planning and immense technical skill, not only saved Iowa and the surrounding states from such an uncontrolled detonation, but achieved a marvel of physical engineering and timing to seamlessly eliminate this threat to public health,” Miller wrote.

“Many thanks as well to Governor Reynolds and Governor-elect Sand and all state and local officials for their cooperation and engagement,” he added. “A tremendous display of unity of effort, purpose and action led by President Trump.”

Sand had expressed concern for days about the proposed detonation, which required many Iowans in the area to evacuate their homes or shelter in place given the threat of lead exposure.

While the governor-elect praised the officials on the ground, he criticized the lead-up to the detonation as “chaotic and unclear.”

“Iowans across the state are understandably alarmed and scared. There must be immediate transparency to understand how and why this situation became what it did,” Sand wrote on X. “Any Iowans who have been impacted in any way must be taken care of fully, right away.”

articles.title: GOP senator calls for vote on pro-labor bill
articles.summary: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is urging Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), his Republican colleague and chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, to move forward on a union-friendly bill that would speed up first contracts for new labor unions. Hawley said in a statement Wednesday that he had previously received a commitment from…
articles.body:
Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) is urging Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.), his Republican colleague and chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, to move forward on a union-friendly bill that would speed up first contracts for new labor unions.

Hawley said in a statement Wednesday that he had previously received a commitment from Cassidy “that a vote on his legislation would occur before the end of this Congress.” Hawley is now calling on Cassidy to schedule that vote.

“We need real labor reform that puts workers first. For too long, mega corporations have denied workers’ rights and refused to meet them in good faith at the bargaining table,” Hawley said in the statement. “Now it is time for Chairman Cassidy to keep his promise to me that the Faster Labor Contracts Act receives a vote in committee before the end of the year. I fully expect the Chairman to honor his word.”

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

A spokesperson for Cassidy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Hawley is an original co-sponsor of the bill, along with Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) and Democratic Sens. Cory Booker (N.J.), Jeff Merkley (Ore.) and Gary Peters (Mich.).

Hawley, who has garnered some attention as a potential 2028 presidential contender, is also a vocal advocate for labor unions in the Republican Party, which traditionally sides with business and industry leaders over unions.

The legislation would authorize government arbitrators to get involved if new unions can’t find agreement with employers within 120 days, preventing employers from stalling negotiations. It has backing from the Teamsters, one of the largest U.S. labor unions.

But the bill moving forward is a red flag for the business community, whch generally supports Republican policies.

The U.S. Chamber of Commerce sent a strongly worded letter opposing the bill in June when the House passed it, arguing it creates an unrealistic timeline that will result in the government negotiating contracts.

“The U.S. Chamber of Commerce strongly opposes the Faster Labor Contracts Act (H.R. 5408), a proposal that could take away workers’ right to vote on the terms and conditions of their own employment by replacing negotiation with forced, government-written contracts,” said Rodney Davis, senior vice president for government affairs, in the letter at the time.

articles.title: New York delays Macy’s Thanksgiving parade because of severe weather
articles.summary: Macy’s pushed the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of a severe storm moving up the East Coast, which is likely to bring heavy rain and wind to the New York City area Thursday. “The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our…
articles.body:
Macy’s pushed the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of a severe storm moving up the East Coast, which is likely to bring heavy rain and wind to the New York City area Thursday.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s said in a statement. “Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized.”

The parade is now scheduled for 8:30 a.m. EST on Saturday morning. This year marks the 100th year of the Thanksgiving Day tradition.

Storms moved from Florida up through the Carolinas Wednesday, expected to have severe impacts in the Washington and New York areas by Thanksgiving Day.

Rain is set to arrive in New York by late Thursday morning, which would have impacted the timing of the parade. One to two inches of rain are expected in New York Thursday, according to the National Weather Service, and the area is under a Coastal Flood Warning from Thursday to Friday morning.

A bigger complication for the parade could have included high wind gusts of up to 55 miles per hour during the day. A primary focal point of the parade is the large balloons, which would not be able to fly properly in a high-wind situation.

Macy’s has never canceled a Thanksgiving Day Parade due to weather, though it did ground balloons during the 1971 parade due to high winds. The parade was canceled for three years, from 1942 through 1944, for World War II. Helium, rubber and other balloon parts were needed for the war effort at the time.

The severe storms moving across the east coast are expected to cause severe travel disruptions and possible flooding. New Jersey’s governor declared a state of emergency Wednesday.

More than 4,000 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed as of Wednesday afternoon, according to flight tracking website FlightAware.

articles.title: Abrego Garcia sees victory in Spain arrival after Trump deportation push
articles.summary: The departure of Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Spain late Tuesday ends an effort of more than a year by the Trump team to deport him to Africa, with both sides claiming victory in the unusual immigration case. His exit caps a nightmarish period for the Maryland man, whose wife and child are U.S. citizens. It…
articles.body:
The departure of Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Spain late Tuesday ends an effort of more than a year by the Trump team to deport him to Africa, with both sides claiming victory in the unusual immigration case.

His exit caps a nightmarish period for the Maryland man, whose wife and child are U.S. citizens.

It spans a wrongful deportation to his native El Salvador in violation of an immigration court order, months in a notorious Salvadoran prison and Justice Department attempts to both prosecute him criminally and deport him to Africa through a civil case.

Abrego Garcia was spotted raising his fist as he exited the airport in Madrid . Speaking with reporters Wednesday, he said he left with his “head held high” after what he described as a remarkably scary period.

“I want to share my joy. I feel happy because I can breathe. I feel free — free of everything evil that I’ve been through and I can breathe freedom,” he said in Spanish on a call with reporters.

“God has given me the understanding and the strength throughout this entire process — because, while I did feel fear at the beginning, I no longer have any fear. I am not afraid to face things, just as I have already faced a government.”

Abrego Garcia entered Spain as a tourist, allowing him to remain in the country for up to 90 days. He traveled with his wife, though she will return to their children in the U.S. at the close of her trip.

Initially deported in March 2025, the Salvadoran migrant spent three months in the massive maximum-security CECOT facility. In the face of court orders and public pressure, the Trump administration brought him back to U.S. soil.

But it quickly ignited a criminal case against him, alleging human trafficking. A judge ultimately dismissed the criminal case as a selective and vindictive prosecution, a rare grant of the claim.

The Justice Department concurrently fought in a civil case to deport him to a series of different African nations, including Liberia.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), who traveled to El Salvador to secure Abrego Garcia’s release, said the Trump administration failed at its aims to leave him in a foreign prison with no due process.

“I’m glad that the Trump administration did not succeed at what they wanted to do. They wanted to leave him to rot there — to rot there for the rest of his life,” the senator said in an emotional press conference.

Both his allies and the Trump administration argued they had won the case.

His attorney, Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, noted Abrego Garcia left as a “free man” to a country of his choice, not deported in shackles on a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) flight.

He also disputed that the Trump administration had achieved its long-held goal of assuring Abrego Garcia “will NEVER be allowed back inside the United States,” as ICE posted on X.

“This is a temporary departure. Mr. Abrego Garcia has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a U.S. citizen spouse and the father of a U.S. citizen child. We don’t expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland,” Sandoval-Moshenberg said in a statement.

“Where he goes from here, where he chooses to settle for the next two years while he waits out the end of this administration, will be his choice, not the administration’s choice. He has a lot of options, and he is still determining them.”

Throughout the saga, Trump officials have repeated a series of false accusations against Abrego Garcia, including that he is a human trafficker — charges a federal judge in Tennessee dismissed as vindictive in May.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin made oft-repeated claims Abrego Garcia was a gang member.

A review by The Hill found the claim was based on a confidential tip from a single informant , who accused Abrego Garcia of being in MS-13’s New York City, a state in which Abrego Garcia has never lived.

In fact, it was gang violence that spurred Abrego Garcia to leave El Salvador. In 2019, an immigration judge cited those grounds in barring him from being sent back to his native country.

“We are DELIGHTED to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported from the United States to Spain,” Mullin wrote on X.

“We promised the American people that this human trafficker, wife beater, gang member, and child predator would not remain in our country. This Salvadoran man will no longer terrorize innocent Americans.”

Immigration advocates and others with ties to Abrego Garcia noted that in the lengthy court battle to deport him to an African country, the Maryland man had pushed to relocate to Costa Rica, which had agreed to accept him as a refugee.

“As much as Mullin seeks to spin this outcome, the Trump admin lost its fight to deport him in shackles to Liberia,” Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X.

“If they had just wanted him to leave, he agreed to be deported to Costa Rica in August 2025. Instead, they wanted him punished harshly. They didn’t get that.”

Van Hollen described his exit as one with “dignity.”

“A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego Garcia to rot in a Salvadoran gulag. Today, Kilmar is traveling to a country of his choice, a free man – unharmed and with dignity,” he said in a statement shortly before Abrego Garcia’s flight.

“While the Trump Administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to countries known for human rights abuses, the Administration was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will and the due process rights guaranteed to him and to all in our nation. I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution.”

The future facing Abrego Garcia is an uncertain one, and his legal team indicated he may only be in Spain temporarily.

His marriage to a U.S. citizen gives him a pathway to citizenship, and his wife has already applied to sponsor him for residency. Abrego Garcia is also the father of a U.S. citizen child, a young boy his attorney described as “severely disabled” with autism.

However, U.S. immigration law imposes a 10-year bar on returning to America given the length of time he was living in the U.S. without authorization.

Sandoval-Moshenberg, speaking with reporters from Spain, said while getting a waiver from that prohibition is routine, he does not expect to secure it while President Trump is in power.

“He would need to receive those waivers from the State Department. We understand that Marco Rubio’s State Department is not giving Kilmar Abrego Garcia any waivers, right? But it is going to be up to the next administration to reunite this family as quickly as possible. … There is an existing immigration pathway. It is a well-trodden immigration pathway,” he said Wednesday.

“Mr. Abrego Garcia is a young man still, right? He’s got a long future ahead of him in Maryland.”

On social media, administration figures attacked Abrego Garcia as well as his chosen destination.

“It’s not surprising this criminal illegal alien would choose to go to Spain, a country that earlier this year was invaded by tens of thousands of illegal aliens,” the Department of Homeland Security wrote on X.

“Spain’s radical open-border policies have made the once-great country a breeding ground for illegal migrants. Good riddance.”

Sandoval-Moshenberg noted that the Trump administration repeatedly tried to deport Abrego Garcia to African nations in spite of the offer from Costa Rica, saying, “You’ve got to understand that there’s a very explicit racism there.”

The attorney said their perseverance in the case was due to Abrego Garcia’s endurance.

He noted that the Trump administration tried to pressure Abrego Garcia to plead guilty to the human trafficking charges in Tennessee in exchange for a chance to leave the country — a deal they thought was unfair but could be his best shot at freedom.

“A lot of folks on the team, to be quite candid, were saying, ‘Look, you know, it’s too big a risk. We can’t — we can’t risk it. You should probably just take this deal.’ And Kilmar said, ‘No, I’m not going to do that. I’m not going to plead guilty to something that I know — fundamentally understand — that I’m not guilty of,” Sandoval-Moshenberg said.

“And he pled not guilty, and here we are a year and a half later, and he has now obtained the precise result that the government was offering him in exchange for a … guilty plea.”

articles.title: Navarro: Democratic probes a recipe for 2028 GOP president or ‘civil war’
articles.summary: Top trade adviser Peter Navarro said likely Democratic investigations into the Trump administration next Congress will lead to Republicans holding the White House in two years or “civil war.” “Congressional Democrats won the midterms on gas and grocery prices. Now, they promise to spend the next two years waging lawfare against Trump officials. That’s a…
articles.body:
Top trade adviser Peter Navarro said likely Democratic investigations into the Trump administration next Congress will lead to Republicans holding the White House in two years or “civil war.”

“Congressional Democrats won the midterms on gas and grocery prices. Now, they promise to spend the next two years waging lawfare against Trump officials. That’s a recipe for either a Republican president in 2029 or civil war. On election night, Senator Ron Wyden [(D-Ore.)] posted one word: ‘Subpoenas,’” Navarro said on a Wednesday episode of Steve Bannon’s “The War Room” show.

“Representative Robert Garcia [(D-Calif.)], set to chair the House Oversight Committee, posted ‘LAWYER UP.’ And Garcia has already sent document retention notices to chief of staff Stephen Miller, Vice President JD Vance and Attorney General Todd Blanche. None of these threats names a crime first,” he added.

Democrats took back the House and Senate in the midterm elections earlier this month, meaning they will now head up key committees in Congress.

Earlier this month, White House counsel Will Scharf vowed that he will battle “tooth and nail” against Democrats in Congress vowing to open expansive probes into the Trump administration next year.

“They can’t investigate for the purpose of inflicting pain on government officials,” Scharf said on “Rob Schmitt Tonight” on Newsmax. “They can’t investigate things for their own self-aggrandizement. These are blatantly inappropriate uses of Congress’s power.”

“We’re going to see what happens in January, but we’re ready to fight tooth and nail here if that’s the road they want to go down,” he added.

Garcia, the incoming chair of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, has advised Trump administration officials they need to “lawyer up.” Last week, Democrats on the committee sent out a dozen letters to President Trump, his family, allies and those with insight to the files linked to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The letters requested their recipients preserve all relevant documents.

For example, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump were asked in their letters about their stake in crypto ventures. Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law, was asked about conflicts of interest as he went ahead with “business pursuits that appear to have allowed you to personally profit from your father-in-law’s presidency on a massive scale.”

The Hill has reached out to Wyden and Garcia’s office for comment.
